supporting_observations.claim: The large outbound transfer was recorded at 13:47:11 UTC, shortly after the alert's approximate 13:46 time: the proxy logged a successful CONNECT to ingest.ironvault-cloud.com with 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes.

Ironvault's agent was running as svc-backup on FILE-COP-01 and was launched by the Services process with a Nightly job targeting https://ingest.ironvault-cloud.com; the proxy and network records attribute the large transfer to that process.

The observed process, account, destination, and transfer size align with the inventory's approved Ironvault offsite backup agent and its expected several-hundred-MB uploads, supporting a benign disposition for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-COP-01 winsec records were not collected from 13:20 to 14:00 UTC because of a log collection outage; domain-controller Security events for that interval are unavailable.
The available transfer records establish the destination, process, and byte count but do not identify or expose the contents of the transferred data.
claims_not_established: The specific files or data included in the upload and whether they were within the intended backup scope.
Whether the backup completed successfully and the uploaded data was intact.
The precise detection trigger or why the alert timestamp is approximately one minute earlier than the recorded upload.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: an unapproved Meridian OpsAgent executable ran on FILE-COP-01 as SYSTEM, then attempted explicit credentials for svc-routes. This is outside the alerted transfer and does not change its disposition (T140-00415, T140-00416, T140-00418).

Separate ticket: sara.ali initiated an RDP session to FILE-COP-01 from WS-SALI-01, although the supplied inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-PBECKER-01 (T140-00491, T140-00492, T140-00499, T140-00502).
